question: The element ‘X’ has seven electrons in outermost shell. Select the group of the modern periodic table to which it belongs.
solution:
The correct answer is __17th group.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The element 'X' with seven electrons in outermost shell belongs to the 17th group of the modern periodic table.
 
• 17th group:
 
 
• It also known as the halogen group.
 
• The halogen group elements have seven electrons in their outermost shell, making them highly reactive and capable of forming compounds with most other elements.
 
• Some of the common halogens include chlorine, fluorine, bromine, iodine, and astatine.
 
• These elements are widely used in various applications such as disinfectants, bleaches, and pharmaceuticals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• 7th group:

 
 
• It has bohrium (Bh), rhenium (Re), technetium (Tc), and manganese (Mn).
 
• Since this group is located on the periodic table's d-block, they are transition metals.
 
• Because it is a part of the larger grouping of transition metals, this group has not given itself a trivial name.
 
• It is frequently referred to as the manganese group or manganese family after its lightest member.
 
• Major group oxidation state (+7) is typical for group 7 elements.
 
 
 
• 16th group:
 
 
• It is known as the chalcogens.
 
• Group 16 is made up of the radioactive elements polonium (Po), livermorium (Lv), oxygen (O), sulphur (S), selenium (Se), and tellurium (Te).
 
• With six valence electrons, the chalcogens are all two electrons away from having a complete outer shell.
 
• The most prevalent oxidation states for them are +4, +6, +2, and −2.
 
 
 
• 18th group:
 
 
• It is known as the noble gases.
 
• The naturally occurring elements of group 18 of the periodic table, namely helium (He), neon (Ne), argon (Ar), krypton (Kr), xenon (Xe), and radon (Rn), are referred to as noble gases.
 
• These chemical elements are colourless, odourless, monatomic gases with cryogenic boiling temperatures and extremely minimal chemical reactivity under normal circumstances.
 
• Because of their "full" outer shell of valence electrons, which prevents them from participating in chemical reactions, noble gases are inert due to their electron configuration.
